note: GLM-4.7-Flash MTP-Q8_0, 2x3 backend x speculation. Second attempt: the first (14:48) lost all six cells to --port 8081 in the variants file while sweep.py polls 8080. A 17.6 GiB model download ran over the network throughout; recorded per CLAUDE.md rather than assumed harmless.

_why: GLM-4.7-Flash-30B-A3B arrived 04.09.2026 as the second candidate on the
operator's throughput axis, after qwen36. setup/env/glm47flash.env carries THREE
flags it cannot justify: the backend, the speculation, and the reasoning
level. This file settles the first two. The third does not exist here.
WHY IT IS A 2x3 AND NOT qwen36's 2x2. This model's file carries its own MTP
head, which qwen36's sweep could not ask about at all - unsloth had dropped
it and there was nothing for -md or --spec-type to point at, so that
question had to be answered afterwards in three separate speed.py runs. Here
the head is in the file being served, so the third speculation arm costs a
cell rather than a run. The extra pair is also the one that matters most on
the evidence: on qwen36 the head moved prose draft acceptance from 4.7 % to
49.2 % and was worth more than every other lever measured.
WHY THE REASONING-LEVEL AXIS IS ABSENT, same as qwen36 and for the same
reason: read 04.09.2026 out of the GGUF's own chat template, this model
knows enable_thinking and clear_thinking and has neither reasoning_effort
nor thinking_budget. There is one thinking setting to measure, not four, and
the profile's enable_thinking:false is carried into every cell rather than
varied - the sweep must not compare two things at once.
THE SPECULATION ARMS ARE CUMULATIVE, and that is deliberate rather than
sloppy. --spec-type accumulates in llama.cpp, so the third arm is
draft-mtp AND ngram-mod. Read against the second arm it therefore says what
the HEAD adds on top of the n-gram drafter, which is the question the
profile has to answer - not what the head is worth in isolation, which no
profile here would ever serve.
THE BUILD DIRECTORIES ARE NAMED, NOT SYMLINKED. build-rocm-patched is a
symlink and what it points at changes; a recorded cell may not. The ROCm arm
names the PINNED build the profile serves from
(build-rocm-cachelookup-b10750-10-g6bbb3eecf), not the house build - because
on qwen36 the house build could not load the MTP file at all, six
llama-bench arms failing in 0 s, and a sweep whose ROCm half simply refused
would have read as a Vulkan victory.
THE VULKAN ARM IS HANDICAPPED AND THE HANDICAP IS KNOWN, carried verbatim
from qwen36's finding: build-vulkan is commit 54ee5ee of 22.08. against the
ROCm arm's b10750-10, on a stack where a build difference has been worth
25 %, and there is no RADV APU heap option set on this machine at all. So a
Vulkan LOSS here is weak evidence and a Vulkan WIN is strong evidence.
-c 65536 throughout, -np 1, f16 KV, no --mmproj: clean single-stream
numbers, and the same window in every cell. -c 65536 rather than the
profile's 202752 for the reason every sweep here uses it - the window is not
the variable, and this model's KV is expensive enough (DERIVED 52.9
KiB/token, 10.2 GiB at the full window) that the full one would buy nothing
and cost GTT in six cells. @MODELS@ and @HOME@ are expanded by
setup/lib/systemdfile.py - never an absolute path, which would tie this file
to one checkout.

THE PORT IS 8080 AND IT IS NOT A FREE CHOICE. bench/sweep.py hard-wires URL = http://127.0.0.1:8080 and polls /slots there; it stops production for the duration, so 8080 is free and there is nothing to sit beside. This file first said 8081 - sideserver's convention, where a second model DOES run beside production - and the sweep of 04.09.2026 reported 'model loaded, but /slots never answered' for the first two cells while the servers were up and answering /slots in 0.7 ms to a curl on 8081. The poller was looking at a port nobody was listening on. Two cells and twenty-five minutes; the failure text names the server, and the server was fine.

variants.name: rocm-nospec
variants.note: The floor: no drafter of any kind. Every other cell is read against this one, and on qwen36 this was the cell Vulkan won by 1.45x.

variants.name: vulkan-nospec
variants.note: The backend, alone. A real question rather than a formality: the answer is model-dependent here and has flipped before - Vulkan won for Laguna without speculation, ROCm won 2x for qwen38 with it, and on qwen36 it SPLIT (Vulkan the unspeculated floor, ROCm everything speculation reached).

variants.name: rocm-ngram
variants.note: The drafter that needs no second model. Read the COPY workload, not just count: this repo once recorded 'the ngram drafters give nothing' from a probe that could not have shown one working (bench/README.md).

variants.name: vulkan-ngram
variants.note: The fourth corner. Not decoration: without it, a backend that wins without speculation and loses with it would look like a single verdict.

variants.name: rocm-mtp
variants.note: The model's own head, on top of the n-gram drafter - the shape setup/env/glm47flash.env starts. Read against rocm-ngram, this says what the HEAD adds. GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1 is part of what is measured here, carried from every other MTP figure in this repo; the other side has never been tried.

variants.name: vulkan-mtp
variants.note: The sixth cell, and the one most likely to fail outright rather than lose: build-vulkan is two weeks older than the ROCm arm and predates several MTP fixes. A failure here is a fact about that build, not about the backend, and has to be reported as one.
